_about: How producers do common jobs in FL Studio (FL 20 and later). Our own notes in plain words. verify=true: some detail (menu wording, version) is unconfirmed.

cards.title: Sidechain compression (kick ducks the bass)
cards.summary: Send the kick's mixer track into the bass track as a sidechain, then put Fruity Limiter in COMP mode on the bass and point its sidechain input at the kick.
cards.why: The bass (or pad) gets quieter for a moment on every kick, so the kick punches through and the mix pumps in time.
steps: Give kick and bass their own mixer tracks.
Select the kick's mixer track.
Right-click the routing arrow at the bottom of the bass track > 'Sidechain to this track'.
On the bass track add Fruity Limiter and switch it to COMP.
Set its SIDECHAIN (SC) number to the kick's input.
Lower threshold until the bass ducks; ratio 4:1-10:1, fast attack, release to taste (shorter = tighter).
settings: 8-12 dB, release timed to the beat (longer)
Duck from a muted kick channel routed only as sidechain (unroute it from master)
tips: The kick still needs its normal route to master - 'Sidechain to this track' adds a sidechain-only send.
Alternatives: Fruity Peak Controller on the kick linked (inverted) to the bass volume; Gross Beat or a volume-shaper preset for a fixed pump curve.
Fruity Compressor has no sidechain input; Fruity Limiter (COMP mode) and Maximus do.
cards.pro: Kick track > right-click target's route arrow > Sidechain to this track; Fruity Limiter COMP mode, SC = source, thresh down, fast att, release to groove. Ghost-kick trigger (unrouted from master) for a clean key. Peak Controller / Gross Beat volume envelopes for fixed curves.

cards.title: Bussing (group tracks into one bus track)
cards.summary: Route several mixer tracks into one bus track instead of master, process them together, and send the bus to master.
cards.why: One fader and one effect chain for the whole drum kit (or all vocals) - easier balance and glue compression.
steps: Pick an empty mixer track for the bus and name it (F2).
Ctrl+click to select the source tracks (e.g. kick, snare, hats).
Right-click the bus track's routing arrow > 'Route to this track only' - they leave master and feed the bus.
Keep the bus routed to master.
Put glue compression / EQ on the bus.
tips: Left-click a routing arrow to ADD a send (keeps existing routes) - that's for parallel sends, not buses.
Colour the bus and its sources the same so the mixer reads at a glance.

cards.title: Send effects (reverb/delay send, parallel compression)
cards.summary: Make a mixer track with a 100%-wet reverb or delay, send several tracks to it at different amounts, and route it to master.
steps: Create a send track, add a reverb (Fruity Reeverb 2, Luxeverb...) and set it fully wet (dry off).
Select a source track, left-click the send track's routing arrow to add a send.
Set the amount with the small knob that appears on the send track's routing arrow.
Repeat for other sources; high-pass the reverb return (~200-300 Hz) to keep lows clean.
tips: Parallel compression: same idea, a heavily compressed copy blended under the dry signal.

cards.title: Rendering stems (one file per mixer track)
cards.summary: In the export window tick 'Split mixer tracks': FL writes one audio file per mixer track that has sound, plus the master.
steps: Name the mixer tracks - file names come from them.
FILE > Export > Wave file..., choose a folder/name.
Tick 'Split mixer tracks' in the export window.
Full song mode, 'Leave remainder' tail, 24-bit WAV.
Decide if master effects should be on the stems (there's an option to disable master effects in recent versions).
tips: Every stem starts at bar 1, so they line up in any DAW.
Bus tracks are rendered as stems too - mute or empty tracks you don't want.

cards.title: Bouncing to audio (freeze a pattern or track)
cards.summary: Turn a synth pattern or a processed track into an audio clip to save CPU or commit to a sound.
steps: Playlist: select the clips, then the clip menu's consolidate / render-to-audio option makes an audio clip of them.
Or: on a mixer track arm it for disk recording, record or export, and drag the file back into the playlist.
Or: add Edison to the mixer track, set it to record on play, play the part and drag the audio out of Edison.
Mute or remove the original pattern clip / channel after checking the bounce.

notes_by_edition.fruity: Fruity Edition can't use audio clips in the playlist (verify for your version) - bounce isn't available there.

cards.title: Recording audio (vocals, guitar)
cards.summary: Choose an ASIO driver, set the input on a mixer track, arm it, press record and pick 'audio into the playlist'.
steps: OPTIONS > Audio settings: your interface's ASIO driver (or FL Studio ASIO), small buffer (64-256).
Select an empty mixer track and choose its audio input (the input selector in the mixer).
Arm the track (record button at the bottom of the mixer track).
Press R (record), choose to record audio into the playlist as an audio clip, then Space.
Stop: the take appears as an audio clip; files go to the user data Recorded folder.
tips: Mono mic = pick a single input (e.g. 'In 1'), not a stereo pair.
Monitor with low latency; turn off heavy plugins while recording.
Loop recording takes: set a loop region and FL stacks takes (options in the record dialog).

notes_by_edition.fruity: No audio recording into the playlist in Fruity Edition (verify); Producer and up have it.

cards.title: Recording MIDI (keyboard into the piano roll)
cards.summary: Enable your keyboard in MIDI settings, select the instrument channel, press record, choose notes (and automation), play.
steps: OPTIONS > MIDI settings: enable the keyboard in Input.
Select the instrument's channel in the channel rack.
Optional: metronome (Ctrl+M), countdown, wait-for-input (Ctrl+I).
Press R, choose notes and automation, then Space and play.
Fix timing with Ctrl+Q (quick quantize) or Alt+Q in the piano roll.
tips: Forgot to hit record? TOOLS > Dump score log to selected pattern recovers what you just played.
Blend recording (Ctrl+B) adds notes on each loop instead of replacing them.

cards.title: Automation (filter sweeps, volume rides)
cards.summary: Right-click any knob > Create automation clip; draw the curve in the playlist clip that appears.
steps: Right-click the knob (or TOOLS > Last tweaked > Create automation clip).
An automation clip spanning the song appears in the playlist.
Right-click in the clip to add points, drag them; right-click a point for curve shapes.
Trim/move the clip like any other; several clips can automate the same knob in different parts.
tips: Recording knob moves: record mode with automation on, then turn the knob while playing.
Between automation clips the knob keeps the last value a clip sent it - start each clip at the value you want.
Same-name rewrite: replace the clip rather than stacking new ones (keeps the channel rack tidy).

cards.title: Slicing and chopping samples
cards.summary: Slicex (Producer+) cuts a loop at its hits and maps slices to keys; Fruity Slicer (every edition) beat-slices to tempo; the playlist slice tool (C) cuts audio clips.
steps: Load the loop into Slicex (drag onto it) - it auto-slices at transients.
Adjust slice markers; each slice plays from its own key.
Dump the slice score to the piano roll to get the original groove, then rearrange the notes.
Quick chop in the playlist: slice tool (C) on an audio clip, move/delete pieces.

notes_by_edition.fruity: Use Fruity Slicer or the channel sampler; Slicex needs Producer Edition or higher.

tips: Edison can also detect beats and send slices to Slicex or the playlist.

cards.title: Pitch correction options by edition
cards.summary: Pitcher (real-time auto-tune) and NewTone (note-by-note editing) come with Signature Bundle and up; lower editions use a third-party tuner or manual clip pitch.
steps: Signature/All Plugins: Pitcher on the vocal track - set key/scale, speed (fast = robotic), formant.
Signature/All Plugins: NewTone - load the vocal, fix notes by dragging them, send back to the playlist.
Fruity/Producer: install a free tuner VST (e.g. MeldaProduction MAutoPitch, Auburn Sounds Graillon free edition) and use it like Pitcher.
Small fixes: split the audio clip and change its pitch (channel settings) per piece.
tips: Correct pitch before heavy compression and reverb.
Producer Edition and up also include Vocodex for robotic/vocoded sounds (not tuning).

cards.title: Making and using your own templates
cards.summary: Set up a project the way you always start, save it in the user data Templates folder, and start new songs from it.
steps: Start blank; add your usual channels, mixer buses, sends and master chain; name and colour everything.
Save as <user data>\Templates\<Category>\<Name>\<Name>.flp.
FILE > New from template > <Category> > <Name>.
Optionally make it the startup template (OPTIONS > General settings).

cards.title: Keeping a project organised
cards.summary: Name and colour channels, mixer tracks, patterns and playlist tracks consistently; route each instrument to its own mixer track; save versions.
steps: F2 names things; right-click > colour (or the colour picker in rename) colours them.
Route each channel to its own mixer track (Ctrl+L) and name the track the same.
One pattern per part (Kick, Bass A, Chords verse...), named.
Group channels with the channel rack's filter groups.
Save new versions as you go (Ctrl+N); remove unused channels and patterns before finishing.
tips: Darker, muted colours stay readable on FL's dark theme; use one colour family per instrument group.

cards.title: Fitting loops and vocals to tempo (time stretching)
cards.summary: An audio clip or sampler channel can stretch to the project tempo: set its original tempo and a stretch mode in its channel settings.
steps: Open the audio clip's channel settings (double-click the clip).
Time / stretch section: set the mode (resample changes pitch; the stretch modes keep pitch).
Right-click the tempo/time knob for 'fit to tempo' or set the loop's original BPM.
Or: Alt+drag the clip edge in the playlist to stretch it to a length (verify).
tips: Drums like a transient-friendly mode; vocals a pitch-preserving mode with formant handling (NewTime gives full control in Signature+).

cards.title: Programming a drum pattern
cards.summary: Load drum samples into channel rack channels, click steps for hits, then refine in the piano roll (velocity, swing, ghost notes).
steps: Drag kick, snare/clap and hat samples onto the channel rack.
Click steps: e.g. kick on 1 and 9, clap on 5 and 13 (16-step bar).
Use the channel rack's swing knob for groove.
Open a channel in the piano roll for rolls, velocity and note lengths.
Put the pattern in the playlist and route each drum to its own mixer track.
tips: FPC gives a pad-based drum kit with layers; good for finger drumming.

cards.title: Exporting MIDI
cards.summary: Whole song: FILE > Export > MIDI file. One part: piano roll menu > File > Export as MIDI file.
steps: Whole song: FILE > Export > MIDI file... (channels become MIDI tracks).
One channel/pattern: open it in the piano roll > File > Export as MIDI file.
tips: Audio clips and effects aren't in a MIDI file; render audio for those.

cards.title: A simple master chain
cards.summary: Keep the master light: gentle EQ, optional glue compression, then a limiter as the very last plugin with its ceiling below 0 dB.
steps: Leave headroom while mixing (master peaks around -6 dB).
Optional: Fruity Parametric EQ 2 for broad tone.
Optional: gentle bus compression (1-2 dB).
Last: Fruity Limiter or Maximus; ceiling about -1 dB for streaming, raise gain to the loudness you want.
Check loudness with a meter (fl-headless finals measure LUFS for you).
tips: Soundgoodizer/Maximus presets are loud quickly but squash dynamics - compare at equal loudness.

cards.title: Checking mono compatibility and stereo width
cards.summary: Fold the master to mono for a moment (Fruity Stereo Shaper or the mixer track's stereo separation knob) to hear what disappears.
steps: Add Fruity Stereo Shaper on the master and choose a mono preset (or turn stereo separation fully to merge).
Listen: parts that vanish or thin out have phase issues or too much width.
Keep kick, bass and lead vocal centred; widen pads and FX instead.
Remove the mono check before exporting.

cards.title: Adding a third-party plugin (VST)
cards.summary: Install the plugin, scan in OPTIONS > Manage plugins, favourite it, then add it from the channel rack '+' (instruments) or a mixer slot (effects).
steps: Install it (VST3 normally goes to Common Files\VST3).
OPTIONS > Manage plugins > Find installed plugins.
Favourite it so it lists in the plugin picker/menus.
Instruments: channel rack '+' > the plugin. Effects: mixer track slot > select > the plugin.

cards.title: Routing channels to mixer tracks
cards.summary: Each channel plays through the mixer track number in its 'Track' box; set it there or select the channel and press Ctrl+L on a free mixer track.
steps: Select the channel(s) in the channel rack.
Select a free mixer track and press Ctrl+L (or type the number in the channel's Track box).
Several at once: Shift+Ctrl+L routes them to consecutive tracks (verify).

cards.title: Stem separation (split a song into vocals/drums/...)
cards.summary: Recent FL versions can split an audio clip into stems (vocals, drums, bass, instruments) from the audio clip's menu.
steps: Put the song in the playlist as an audio clip.
Open the clip's menu and choose the stem separation option.
Pick which stems; FL adds them as new clips/tracks.

cards.title: Layering instruments (play several sounds from one part)
cards.summary: The Layer channel triggers several channels at once from one set of notes; or copy the notes to each channel's pattern.
steps: Add the Layer plugin to the channel rack.
Select the channels to layer, then in Layer click 'Set children'.
Write notes on the Layer channel; all children play.

cards.title: Markers, loops and song sections
cards.summary: Add time markers in the playlist's time line to name sections; drag in the time line to set a loop/selection.
steps: Right-click (or the time line menu) in the playlist time line > Add marker (Alt+T, verify).
Rename it (Verse, Chorus...).
Drag across the time line to select a region; playback loops it.
Marker menu has loop/start/pause and time-signature types.
